title: The Kiln That Drinks the Night
story: Deep in a cliffside glassworks, Threnavar the Moonglass Kiln-Wyrm has curled around the village's great kiln and swallowed the heat-vent, so the molten moonglass is cooling into a useless lump. The glassblowers can pour the glass only while it is above 900 degrees, and right now it reads 1,260 degrees. Mr 6 adjusts his little helmet, borrows a chalk slate, and starts timing the drop.
question: The glass cools 24 degrees every minute, but Mr 6's bellows crew adds back 9 degrees every minute. How many minutes until the glass falls from 1,260 degrees to 900 degrees?
solution: The real cooling rate is 24 - 9 = 15 degrees lost each minute.
360 / 15 = 24 minutes before the moonglass is too cold to pour.
praise: Tracking the temperature drop was exactly the right move — the missing step was subtracting the bellows' 9 degrees back out first.
hint: The glass loses 24 but gains 9 each minute. What is the true loss per minute?
victory: Threnavar uncoiled in a huff, hissing that nobody had ever out-timed him before, and the villagers poured a moonglass window so bright the wyrm stayed to admire his own reflection.
imagePrompt: A long glass-scaled wyrm coiled around a glowing cliffside kiln at night while a small knightly numeral 6 in a blue cape marks a countdown on a chalk slate, orange firelight against cold blue moonlight.
